## National Ignition Facility Experiment Achieves Fusion Ignition

A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory experiment at the National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition on December 5, 2022. The U.S. Department of Energy announced the result on December 13.

The experiment delivered 2.05 megajoules of energy to its target and generated 3.15 megajoules of fusion energy. That comparison applies at the target: it does not measure net electricity delivered to the grid or account for the facility’s overall electricity use. DOE presented the achievement as progress toward inertial fusion energy, while noting that many scientific and technological developments are still needed for practical energy production.
